steps.title: Assess fecal bolus suitability
steps.instruction: Locate the fecal bolus and determine if it is suitable for collection: do not collect if you cannot distinguish interior from exterior, if it is heavily contaminated with leaves/soil, if it has been stepped on or splattered, or if the bolus (or 2‑3 large pieces) is shorter than the distance from your middle knuckle to the tip of your pointer finger.

steps.title: Remove external debris
steps.instruction: Using a wooden spatula, carefully remove leaves, sticks, vegetative debris, and soil from the outside of the bolus as much as possible.

steps.title: Record field data
steps.instruction: Fill in the field data sheet with the collection time, GPS coordinates, age/sex class (AM, AF, SM, J), individual ID if known, any unique physical marks (e.g., bent digits, bald spots), and any sample irregularities such as blood, mucus, or worms. Add any extra information on the notes sheet and ensure the sample ID matches across sheets.

steps.title: Seal and label transport glove
steps.instruction: Place the remaining feces in a disposable glove, seal the glove for transport, and label the glove with the sample ID code using a Sharpie marker. Avoid excessive squashing of the sample.

steps.title: Collect DNA sub‑sample in RNAlater
steps.instruction: Find the pointy end of the bolus (the last part expelled). From the outer layer of this end, scrape off approximately 2 mL of feces with a wooden spatula and place it into 4 mL of RNAlater in an 8 mL tube.

steps.title: Weigh DNA tube and calculate fecal mass
steps.instruction: Weigh the 8 mL tube containing RNAlater and the 2 mL fecal sub‑sample; record this “DNA‑tube w/ sample mass” on the lab data sheet. Subtract the known tube + RNAlater mass (recorded separately) to obtain the fecal mass in the DNA tube.

steps.title: Weigh entire fecal bolus
steps.instruction: Place a sheet of weigh paper on the scale, tare it, then carefully invert the glove containing the whole bolus onto the paper and record the total bolus mass on the lab data sheet.

steps.title: Prepare lab data sheet with masses
steps.instruction: Enter for each sample the ID code, date, tube number, tube + RNAlater mass, DNA‑tube w/ sample mass, and calculated DNA sample mass. Leave the total mass and DNA sample mass columns blank for later calculation.

steps.title: Measure 1 g ethanol sub‑sample (OH)
steps.instruction: Tare an 8 mL collection tube labeled “OH” on the scale. Using a flame‑sterilized spatula, add feces until the mass is 1 g ± 0.1 g (acceptable range 0.9–1.1 g). Record the exact mass on the lab sheet under “Mass OH”. Fill the tube completely with 96 % ethanol, noting any major sample loss or abnormalities.

steps.title: Measure two 3 g formalin sub‑samples (F1/F2)
steps.instruction: Using the same method, measure two sub‑samples of approximately 3 g each into tubes labeled “F1” and “F2”. Record each mass under “Mass F1” and “Mass F2”. Fill each tube with 10 % formalin so that no air remains. Acceptable range for a 3 g sample is 2.9–3.1 g. If you cannot obtain two full 3 g samples, place one full 3 g sample in F1, then place the remaining feces in F2 and record the actual mass of F2.

steps.title: Label all collection tubes
steps.instruction: Using labeling tape, affix a label to each tube: ID code + reagent code (OH, F1, F2). For formalin tubes add a “1” or “2” after the “F” to indicate first or second 3 g sub‑sample (e.g., VA‑03JUN‑4F1, VA‑03JUN‑4F2). Label the DNA tube with the ID code followed by “D”. Avoid getting ethanol on the outside of the tube; if ink smears, dry and re‑label.

steps.title: Seal caps with parafilm and store
steps.instruction: Cut a parafilm strip approximately 1.5 in long and 1 in wide. Stretch slightly and wrap around the tube cap, covering the side of the cap and about 0.5 in of the tube. Store all tubes upright in sample boxes labeled with the project name (Johnston GM fecal samples), location, and reagent code (D, OH, F1, F2). Keep boxes at room temperature, in a dark location, ensuring air pockets remain at the top of each tube.

steps.title: Document and archive data sheets
steps.instruction: When all data sheets for a set of samples are complete, photograph or scan them and email the digital copies to project leads weekly. Store the physical sheets together in chronological order in a dry place and make a photocopy for backup.

steps.title: Manage data‑sheet sets per group
steps.instruction: Use one complete set of field, lab, and notes sheets per monkey group. If a set fills up, start a new set for that group, marking the first set “1/2” and the new set “2/2”. Write all entries in pen, cross out mistakes and continue on the next line (do not overwrite). Verify that the sample ID on every container matches the ID on all data sheets.
